extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Official submission rules and quality/format requirements for posting articles to arXiv, covering accepted file formats, figures, metadata, filenames, licensing, announcement timing, and submission procedures. Intended to guide authors on what is acceptable and how submissions are processed and announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitters only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information; authors must use their arXiv account to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute, or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required at submission; ensure you understand and accept the distribution license or provide an alternative license that conveys equivalent distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv's goal is portable/stable formats — TeX/LaTeX is preferred because it is open and does not hide information. Note that arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Users of word processors (pre-Word 2007) should save as PDF. Scanned documents are not accepted regardless of format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Scanned documents are not accepted in any format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned PDFs or images of pages are explicitly rejected — submit source or proper PDF instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be in common formats such as PostScript (PS/EPS) for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photographic images, GIF or PNG for non-photographic bitmaps, and PDF figures only with PDFLaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate formats for the figure type. PDF figures are only accepted when using PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures must be included and not omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections; abstract-only submissions are also not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you can host figures elsewhere, do not omit them from the submission — submissions with missing elements will be rejected as unhelpful to readers and of limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce large figure/file sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make efforts to reduce file sizes before submission; see arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard LaTeX graphics packages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv administration cannot provide TeX-related help; seek assistance from colleagues for TeX issues to ensure figures render correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other character (spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename case sensitivity and matching internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv's system (e.g., Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match file name case exactly regardless of whether your local system is case sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; plan accordingly because support is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (metadata) preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Title/abstract information is prepared separately and used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions on preparing title/abstract metadata; ensure this information is accurate and well-formatted because it is publicly displayed and used for discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read system messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Before finalizing 'Submit Article', check both the title/abstract metadata and the processed files; read any messages returned by the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them before final submission or contact administrators for unresolved problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit option for pre-announcement corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement you may select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting takes the article out of the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time. Edits before public announcement will not generate additional versions; the date stamp is the time the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit/replace rather than resubmit for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum; replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to update and make corrections to articles by replacing the original submission rather than creating duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and announcement scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are normally announced on a daily schedule; each day's submissions before 16:00 US Eastern time (Mon–Fri) are made publicly available after 20:00 US Eastern time that day (with no activity scheduled on weekends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided for how submission time affects availability and mailing listings. Be aware edits and final submission times determine announcement order and that edits can delay appearance to the next day's announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission order determined by final submission time
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected at the end of the submission process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset this time and change position in the listings. Edits permitted between 16:00 and the 20:00 announcement time will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must submit themselves (responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions; third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged and often cause problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv encourages authors to take responsibility for submissions — third-party submissions are more likely to have errors or mismatches in metadata and other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional affiliation and report numbers required
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided and official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate affiliations and any applicable institutional report numbers as part of submission metadata.
